title: Deportation Flights to Libya, Colombia, Guatemala — Third-Country Removals Expand
description_short: Deportation Flights to Libya, Colombia, Guatemala — Third-Country Removals Expand
description_medium: On May 7, 2025, a federal judge temporarily blocked the planned removal of Asian migrants to Libya or another third country. Attorneys said the migrants, from countries including the Philippines, Vietnam and Laos, faced removal without a reasonable-fear screening or a chance to challenge an adverse finding. Libya’s internationally recognized government denied agreeing to receive them.
description_long: On May 7, 2025, a federal judge issued a temporary restraining order preventing the government from sending migrants to Libya or any other third country. The planned group included people from the Philippines, Vietnam and Laos, according to the linked NBC News report. Their attorneys had asked the court to intervene, arguing that the migrants were being prepared for removal without a reasonable-fear screening and without the time to challenge a negative finding. The attorneys also alleged that some detainees were pressured to sign documents agreeing to go to Libya; that account came from their court filing. Libya’s Government of National Unity said it had no agreement with the United States to receive deportees and rejected using the country as a destination without its consent. The order blocked the proposed removals while the court considered the challenge; the report does not say the migrants were flown to Libya. The supplied title also names Guatemala and Colombia, separate episodes not established by this linked report, so the broader timeline needs supporting sources before the entry can be marked complete.

title: Laura Loomer Triggers Mass Purge of National Security Council Staff
description_short: Laura Loomer Triggers Mass Purge of National Security Council Staff
description_medium: In early April 2025, Laura Loomer visited the Oval Office and presented President Trump with allegations that National Security Council staff were disloyal. The administration then dismissed at least 15 officials, including senior staff in intelligence, technology and legislative affairs. A later round of firings under Marco Rubio in May widened the personnel changes, according to the supplied account.
description_long: In early April 2025, far-right activist and conspiracy theorist Laura Loomer visited the Oval Office and presented President Trump with a dossier accusing National Security Council staff of disloyalty to MAGA. Trump, furious, directed National Security Adviser Mike Waltz to fire them on the spot. At least 15 NSC officials were dismissed in the first wave—including senior directors overseeing intelligence, technology, and legislative affairs. By April 24, Reuters confirmed at least 20 firings total, leaving sections overseeing Latin America, legislative affairs, and international organizations largely unstaffed. Loomer, who has promoted QAnon-adjacent theories, openly took credit on social media. On May 23, 2025, a second mass termination swept the NSC as Secretary of State Marco Rubio (by then interim National Security Adviser) fired dozens more staff covering nearly every major geopolitical issue, from Ukraine to Kashmir. The administration aimed to shrink the NSC to just a few dozen people. Former national security officials described the gutting as catastrophic for institutional knowledge and America's ability to coordinate complex foreign policy responses.

title: SEC Drops 60%+ of Crypto Enforcement Cases in Mass Regulatory Capitulation
description_short: SEC Drops 60%+ of Crypto Enforcement Cases in Mass Regulatory Capitulation
description_medium: A New York Times review found that the SEC eased up on more than 60% of crypto matters pending when Trump returned to office. The pullback included dismissals, pauses, reduced penalties and other changes. The finding describes a broad enforcement retreat; it does not mean that every affected case was dropped.
description_long: Within weeks of Trump's inauguration, the Securities and Exchange Commission under acting chair Mark Uyeda began systematically dropping enforcement actions against the crypto industry, which had spent more than $100 million supporting Trump's election. By February 21, 2025, the SEC dismissed its nearly two-year case against Coinbase, the largest U.S. crypto exchange, which had been charged with operating as an unregistered securities exchange. On March 20, 2025, the SEC dropped its four-year case against Ripple Labs and its XRP token. The agency also dropped or froze cases against Kraken, Gemini, Binance, and Robinhood. A December 2025 New York Times investigation found that the SEC had eased up on more than 60% of the crypto cases that were in progress at the start of Trump's second term — a retreat from a single industry with no legal precedent. The investigation into Justin Sun, who had invested $45 million in Trump's World Liberty Financial, was settled in March 2025 for $10 million with no admission of wrongdoing, after being paused following his WLF investment. Senator Elizabeth Warren demanded explanations for the apparent connection between Sun's investment in the Trump family business and the SEC's decision to drop its case against him. The mass regulatory pullback directly enriched the crypto industry that had funded Trump's election while benefiting the Trump family, which held billions in crypto assets subject to SEC oversight.

title: RFK Jr.'s HHS Unleashes Anti-Vaccine Conspiracy Orthodoxy, Triggers Worst Measles Crisis in 33 Years
description_short: RFK Jr.'s HHS Unleashes Anti-Vaccine Conspiracy Orthodoxy, Triggers Worst Measles Crisis in 33 Years
description_medium: In June 2025, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 members of the CDC’s vaccine advisory committee and said he would replace the panel, Reuters reported. The committee advises the CDC on vaccine recommendations. The membership change altered who served on the body; the linked report does not establish that it caused later measles cases.
description_long: In 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. — who had spent decades falsely linking vaccines to autism and claiming government cover-up of vaccine injury data — was given full authority over the nation's public health apparatus, with catastrophic results. On June 9, 2025, Kennedy fired all 17 members of the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the independent scientific body that had shaped vaccine recommendations for decades, calling for a clean sweep and pledging to replace members with his own loyalists; he had already changed COVID-19 vaccine recommendations without consulting the committee. Kennedy's HHS canceled a $766 million Moderna H5N1 vaccine contract, required federally funded schools and clinics to accept religious and conscience-based exemptions to vaccine mandates, and shelved government promotional campaigns for flu shots in favor of messaging about informed consent. By July 31, 2025, CDC data showed kindergarten MMR vaccination rates fell to 92.5% — below the 95% herd immunity threshold — with vaccine exemptions reaching an all-time high of 3.6%; Idaho reached 15.4% exemption rates. Measles cases hit 1,333 confirmed cases in 2025, the highest count since the disease was declared eliminated in 2000, with a child dying of measles in rural West Texas in February 2025 — the first U.S. measles death in a decade. NBC News found that 77% of U.S. counties had experienced notable vaccination rate declines since 2019, with 67% of counties now below herd immunity levels for measles.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Gaza Ethnic Cleansing Plan: Trump Proposes Expelling 2 Million Palestinians to Egypt and Jordan
description_short: Gaza Ethnic Cleansing Plan: Trump Proposes Expelling 2 Million Palestinians to Egypt and Jordan
description_medium: In January and February 2025, President Trump proposed that Egypt and Jordan permanently take in Palestinians from Gaza, later saying Palestinians had no alternative but to leave. He also said the United States would take over Gaza and rebuild it. Egypt and Jordan rejected the proposal; the linked reporting describes a plan under discussion, not a transfer that occurred.
description_long: On January 25, 2025, President Donald Trump told reporters he wanted to “clean out” Gaza and have Egypt and Jordan permanently absorb its more than two million Palestinian residents. He described Gaza as a mess and said Palestinians could be moved to a beautiful new place. On February 4, standing beside Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Trump said Palestinians had no alternative but to leave and proposed that the United States take over Gaza and rebuild it as a “Riviera of the Middle East.” The proposal would have moved a population displaced by the war outside its territory, making the prospect of permanent removal central to the debate. Egypt and Jordan rejected the proposal, and Reuters reported that regional governments had objected to relocating Palestinians from Gaza. Human Rights Watch characterized the remarks as an alarming escalation of forced displacement and ethnic cleansing. The proposal did not result in a relocation; Egypt and Jordan rejected it. An Israeli minister welcomed the idea and said he was preparing an operational plan, but that statement likewise did not establish implementation. The episode put the proposed removal of Gaza’s population and the governments’ response at the center of international criticism.

title: Bankrupt Again: Trump Hotels Files Fourth Chapter 11 in 2004
description_short: Bankrupt Again: Trump Hotels Files Fourth Chapter 11 in 2004
description_medium: In November 2004, Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New Jersey with about $1.8 billion in debt. The restructuring covered the company’s Atlantic City casinos, which faced new competition and high interest costs. The filing was by the corporation, not a personal bankruptcy by Donald Trump.
description_long: In November 2004, Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Camden, New Jersey, listing approximately $1.8 billion in debt — the company's second federal bankruptcy filing. Trump's three Atlantic City casinos had been devastated by new competition while carrying debt at 15 percent interest; the restructuring aimed to cut debt by $500 million and reduce interest rates to 8 percent. Trump personally retained a management fee and maintained influence over the properties despite the bankruptcy, and publicly spun the filing as a standard business maneuver, stating he used the laws of this country and made a lot of money. The same casinos would file for bankruptcy yet again in February 2009, marking the third time that specific casino company entered Chapter 11, with combined assets of $2.1 billion against debts of $1.74 billion.
